conventions.ordering: all list outputs in ascending id unless stated
conventions.via_labels: each unread id maps to its sources: `pin:<pin id>` or `requires:<the envelope whose requires edge pulled it in>`
conventions.version_resolution: every requirement resolves to the current version of its lineage before the ack check — an ack on a superseded version does not cover (4.4)
conventions.onboard_R32: `canon` is the whole set in force for that identity, in id order, each entry marked `read` at the document's CURRENT version and carrying the `via` that put it there. `unread` is the subset with no such ack and keeps its prior meaning exactly: a conforming client fetches documents from `unread`, never from `canon`. A board that widens `unread` to the full set passes every positive check here and still charges every returning session a re-download of canon it has already acked.

checks.why: R32: e1 acked the full closure at 15, so `unread` is empty — and the canon set still comes back, every entry marked `read: true`. Empty unread means NOTHING HAS CHANGED, not that there is nothing; a board serving only the unread subset makes those two states indistinguishable from a broken reduction. 10 still reports truncation: its requires -> 9 sits one past max_required_depth 2.

the full load-in for an identity with no acks: both pinned docs plus the requires chain 12 -> 11 -> 10; 9 is past the depth horizon and 10 is reported truncated rather than the cap being silent. R32: `canon` and `unread` name the same four ids here, every entry `read: false` — for a fresh identity the two lists coincide, which is exactly why a fresh-board suite cannot see the difference between them.

acks voided by canon supersession: 19 superseded 8, the pin follows the lineage, and exactly the changed document reappears — nothing else. R32 makes that visible in one picture rather than by inference: `canon` shows 10, 11, 12 still `read: true` beside 19 `read: false`, so a reader sees WHICH document moved instead of a bare list of one.
the unmet closure for acting on one envelope: the job's own requires (the motivating rake) plus the nest's canon pin.
e1 drained the reading list at 24; the CLAIM at 25 is accepted because this closure is empty.
the kb migration ran the whole require_acks gauntlet and closed clean.
the graduation ceremony as a job-board lifecycle: the delivery that closes the JOB is the POLICY itself (R15) — request, claim, ruling, all attributable.
stable across the graduation: the /atlas/jobs pin target (21) is acked, only the unre-read canon v2 remains.
